title: Refraction and Total Internal Reflection

final_note: Above the critical angle, no light escapes — that is fibre optics in one sentence.

concepts.def: n = c / v in the medium.
n1 sin theta1 = n2 sin theta2.
Angle giving theta2 = 90°: sin theta_c = n2/n1.

Glass guide using TIR to keep light inside.

walkthroughs.body_html: n = speed of light in vacuum / speed in medium. Always n >= 1. Light slows when entering a denser medium, bending towards the normal.
n1 sin(theta1) = n2 sin(theta2). Travelling into a denser medium (higher n), theta decreases. Into a less dense medium, theta increases.
For light going from denser to less dense (n1 > n2), if theta1 > theta_c where sin(theta_c) = n2/n1, the light fully reflects internally. This traps light in fibres.
